evaluation.title: Evaluation pipeline
evaluation.caption: Freeze the task distribution before comparing candidates. Keep test evidence separate from tuning.
nodes: Version cases, expected outcomes, provenance, and development/test membership.
Record model, prompt, decoding, tool, and corpus versions.
Use the same cases and budgets for a paired comparison.
Apply exact checks, functional tests, retrieval metrics, and calibrated judgment separately.
Require slice-level non-regression, confidence intervals, latency, cost, and security checks.

judge.title: LLM-as-a-Judge calibration
judge.caption: The judge is another measured component. Its score is not ground truth.
nodes: Create an adjudicated calibration subset and document disagreement.
Hide candidate identity; evaluate both answer orders and include ties.
Use a fixed rubric with structured scores and evidence references.
Compare against human labels and quantify order, verbosity, and self-preference bias.
Inspect disagreements on development data. Keep held-out cases untouched.

rag.title: Advanced retrieval architecture
rag.caption: Lexical and dense retrieval run in parallel; rank fusion and reranking narrow the evidence set.
nodes: Carry user access scope, temporal constraints, identifiers, and intent.
Retrieve exact terminology through a lexical index.
Retrieve embedding neighbors; measure ANN recall separately.
Fuse ranks, rerank a candidate pool, and retain evidence IDs.
Select within a token budget and cite the original source offsets.

context.title: Context engineering
context.caption: The context window is a constrained working set. Source trust and relevance remain separate.
nodes: Trusted instructions define the task and output contract.
Untrusted documents carry citations, revisions, and timestamps.
Version memory, enforce expiry, and preserve unresolved evidence.
Reserve output space; select, compress, and order task-relevant evidence.
Separate instructions from evidence; verify answers against provenance.

loop.title: Bounded agent loop
loop.caption: The model proposes actions. Application code validates, authorizes, executes, and terminates.
nodes: Restore observations and remaining step, token, and time budgets.
Return a typed action or final response. Invalid decisions do not execute.
Check schema, identity, permissions, destination, and budget.
Enforce timeout and idempotency; return a structured observation.
Persist results, reconcile failures, and stop or escalate on terminal conditions.

react.title: ReAct: observation changes the next action
react.caption: Inspectable task state and actions support debugging; a model rationale alone is not evidence.
nodes: Set the goal and explicit completion criteria.
Choose a tool using the current evidence and remaining budget.
Record evidence IDs, uncertainty, and missing information.
Terminate with supported claims or a clear evidence gap.

mcp.title: MCP host, clients, and servers
mcp.caption: Capability discovery is not authorization. The host and tools still enforce access policy.
nodes: Own user interaction, consent, state, and tool policy.
Maintain a connection to the document server and validate results.
Maintain a separate connection to the metrics server.
Expose scoped search and fetch capabilities over the chosen transport.
Expose authenticated deterministic calculations, rate limits, and logs.
Servers authorize access to resources; reject unsafe identifiers and destinations.

workflow.title: Workflow vs agent
workflow.caption: Control-flow ownership determines the pattern. Choose using measured task variability and failure cost.
nodes: Use a workflow when valid transitions are known in advance.
Typed conditions choose the next step; individual steps may call an LLM.
Check each output contract and preserve deterministic calculations.
Use an agent only when evidence-dependent action choice adds value.
A bounded policy loop selects the next permitted action.
Application code still controls permissions, budgets, and escalation.

planner.title: Planner–executor system
planner.caption: A plan is a typed dependency structure with acceptance criteria, not an unbounded to-do list.
nodes: Capture scope, budget, constraints, and completion criteria.
Create tasks, dependencies, evidence requirements, and stop rules.
Run permitted tools and persist observations for each task.
Check task evidence and report gaps without rewriting the plan silently.
Bound replans; terminate when criteria pass or escalate if resources are exhausted.

multi.title: Multi-agent coordination
multi.caption: Isolate worker context and combine evidence explicitly. More agents add coordination failure modes.
nodes: Assign bounded work and own termination and failure handling.
Invoke deterministic analytics and report units and data revisions.
Deduplicate claims, preserve contradictions, and retain provenance.
Check completeness and support; missing workers do not imply successful completion.

security.title: Security boundaries
security.caption: Untrusted content never grants permissions. Enforce access before the side effect.
nodes: Documents, news, tool output, and memory can contain hostile instructions.
Label provenance and keep instructions separate from retrieved data.
Treat model output as an untrusted request.
Check caller, operation, arguments, destination, and least privilege.
Bind approval to exact arguments; enforce idempotency and log the result.
Denied operations do not execute; record redacted evidence for investigation.

adaptation.title: Fine-tuning vs RAG decision framework
adaptation.caption: Test the simplest baseline first. Retrieval and adaptation can address different failure modes.
nodes: Use evaluation slices to identify what is actually failing.
Changing facts and source grounding suggest retrieval or tools.
Consistent task behavior may benefit from examples or adaptation.
Measure evidence recall and grounded answer quality.
Compare prompts before training; check held-out gains and retention.
Keep the combination only if evidence supports added cost and complexity.

inference.title: Inference architecture
inference.caption: Separate admission, scheduling, prefill, and decode to explain latency and saturation.
nodes: Authenticate, rate-limit, select a model, and enforce request budgets.
Admit requests subject to memory and latency constraints.
Process prompt tokens and populate keys and values.
Generate tokens using cached attention state until completion.
Measure TTFT and complete latency; track cancellations and errors.

kv.title: KV cache and continuous batching
kv.caption: Finished sequences free slots; new requests can join subsequent decoding iterations.
nodes: Arrival rate and prompt lengths determine queue pressure.
Schedule sequences for the next iteration under a memory budget.
Cache per-layer keys and values for each sequence; memory grows with retained tokens.
Reuse cached states and append new token states.
Release completed sequences and admit waiting requests; track fairness and tail latency.

durable.title: Durable workflow
durable.caption: Persist state and reconcile effects. At-least-once delivery requires application-level idempotency.
nodes: Assign stable event identity; duplicates are expected.
Persist workflow state before acknowledging progress.
Run bounded tools and verify evidence; persist the result.
Pause durably; expire approval and bind it to an exact action.
Use idempotency keys and reconcile unknown outcomes before retry.
Resume from checkpoints; back off transient failures and quarantine poison events.

telemetry.title: OpenTelemetry across a request
telemetry.caption: Carry trace context through the queue. Observe model and tool calls without exposing secrets.
nodes: Create the request trace with a safe request ID and release revision.
Propagate context or link asynchronous work; record queue delay.
Record model, tokens, latency, prompt version, and outcome.
Record tool identity, retries, authorization outcome, and redacted errors.
Export traces, metrics, and logs with redaction and sampling policy.
Monitor success, latency, errors, and cost attribution by release and task slice.

production.title: Production AI platform
production.caption: The synchronous entry point and durable execution path share policy, evidence, and telemetry.
nodes: Validate inputs, authenticate users, rate-limit, and enforce budgets.
Route simple cases; enqueue long-running work with stable IDs.
Use typed MCP tools, bounded state, and provider fallbacks.
Persist provenance, workflow checkpoints, and access-scoped data.
Check material claims and consequential actions before release.
Feed measured failures into regression tests and staged releases.

project1.title: Project 1 · Evidence-first research
project1.caption: The verifier reports support status independently; the writer retains claim-level provenance.
nodes: Return subquestions, search strategy, evidence requirements, and completion criteria.
Retrieve webpages, PDFs, structured data, and repository files through scoped tools.
Normalize sources and maintain supports/contradicts relationships.
Check each material claim: supported, partial, contradicted, or insufficient.
Write a report with evidence references, contradictions, limitations, and no invented support.
Use 80–100 questions and compare a single agent to planner/researcher/verifier.

project2.title: Project 2 · Market intelligence and risk
project2.caption: Calculations and risk rules stay deterministic. Consequential notifications require approval.
nodes: Validate prices, filings, news, timestamps, units, revisions, and provenance.
Calculate returns, volatility, z-scores, correlations, and volume anomalies in code.
Use authenticated MCP tools; separate numerical evidence from hypotheses.
Return severity, confidence, supporting and contradictory evidence, and escalation.
Bind human approval to the exact report action; deduplicate dispatch and audit.
Persist events and workflow state, collect spans, and evaluate ≥150 scenarios.
